headline.title: Dave Eggers told OpenAI staff that ChatGPT was ‘silencing an entire generation’
headline.summary: Author Dave Eggers expressed concerns to OpenAI staff that ChatGPT could be "silencing an entire generation" during a talk last year. His remarks highlighted the potential impact of AI on creative expression and the arts.

articles.title: Kimi: Threat or menace?
articles.summary: Moonshot AI has launched an updated version of its Kimi model, raising alarms regarding potential implications for "full AI communism." The release has sparked discussions about the ethical and societal impacts of advanced AI technologies.

articles.title: A Red Line and Oversight Framework for Government AI Contracts
articles.summary: The article discusses the development of a framework for government AI contracts that establishes clear boundaries for acceptable use cases, such as prohibiting autonomous targeting without human oversight while permitting applications like missile defense. It emphasizes the importance of mechanism design and negotiation strategies to optimize the framework against organizational constraints.

articles.title: The apps, gadgets, and tools every reader needs
articles.summary: The article provides a curated list of essential apps, gadgets, and tools for readers, highlighting the best options available in the current market. It serves as a resource for those looking to enhance their reading experience with technology.

articles.title: Your Period Tracker Is (Probably) Spying on You
articles.summary: A recent investigation reveals that many period tracking apps may be collecting and sharing sensitive user data without proper consent. The article also highlights other cybersecurity concerns, including Russian hackers targeting infrastructure and a breach involving an AI music generator.

articles.title: How Google’s New Gemini Rates Work and How to Track Your Usage
articles.summary: Google has updated its Gemini usage quotas, resulting in potentially fewer AI responses for users. The article explains the new rating system and provides guidance on how to monitor your usage effectively.

articles.title: Endogenous Alignment
articles.summary: The article discusses the process of aligning children's behavior to adult values, starting around the age of one, primarily through exogenous methods such as rewards and punishments. It highlights how operant conditioning leverages children's instinctive behaviors to encourage desirable actions and discourage undesirable ones.

articles.title: Vertu wants executives to pay $6,880 for an AI agent — here’s how it actually performs
articles.summary: Vertu is offering its luxury foldable smartphone equipped with an AI agent for $6,880, highlighting features such as AI workflows, battery life, and security. The article provides an in-depth look at the device's performance and user experience in daily use.

articles.title: Prompt Injection Attacks Are Thwarting AI Hacking Agents
articles.summary: Researchers have developed a technique called "context bombing" to prevent malicious AI agents from executing harmful actions by tricking them into shutting down. This method addresses the rising threat of prompt injection attacks aimed at exploiting AI systems.

articles.title: Databricks hits $188B valuation, extending its run as AI’s favorite second act
articles.summary: Databricks has achieved a valuation of $188 billion as it transforms into an AI-focused company, emphasizing the cost benefits of open weight AI models for coding in its recent research. The company's shift highlights its growing prominence in the AI sector.

articles.title: Should we benchmark conceptual capabilities using judgment prediction tasks?
articles.summary: The article discusses the challenges of using subjective judgment prediction tasks to benchmark AI capabilities, suggesting that these tasks may not effectively measure AI performance. It proposes an alternative approach where AIs are instructed to predict specific individuals' judgments on complex issues, such as the likelihood of an AI takeover.

articles.title: Neil Rimer thinks the AI money is coming back out
articles.summary: Venture capitalist Neil Rimer, co-founder of Index Ventures, forecasts that the wealth generated by AI in Silicon Valley will need to be redistributed, whether through voluntary means or otherwise. His comments reflect ongoing discussions about the economic impact of AI advancements.
